answers.answer: No. The 80-86% gross margin is the gross-margin vanity trap and is NEVER quoted as evidence the venture works (SCOPE_GLOSSARY rule #8; conflicts_and_dominance 'gross vs contribution after CAC'). Contribution margin after CAC is the viability metric, and CAC governs survival, not factory cost. The correct posture is GATED-conditional-GO, not a naive GO: the venture is dead as first drawn (value-led, A2-acrylic-hero, cold paid social); exactly one inverted configuration closes the math (A3-led + 2-unit bundles to AOV ~$120-150, organic/community/affiliate acquisition, bulk IOR -> CA 3PL, own nothing but design + brand + import); and inventory/dye-lot cash is FORBIDDEN until the four hard gates pass. The single tie-breaker is live blended CAC [UNKNOWN], which must clear under ~$35 organic-led and be measured by the $1-2k live-ad test FIRST. So: VIABLE only in that narrow configuration and only if the gates pass; confidence is HIGH that it is GATED, LOW-to-UNKNOWN that it clears.

answers.answer: Walk-through for a $6 ex-factory acrylic A2 (labeled [ESTIMATE]; the ex-factory leg's width rests on the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate, so this is band arithmetic, not a hard actual): (1) ex-factory transaction value $6. (2) Classify by chief weight: acrylic = MMF, heading 6110.30.30, MFN ~32% [FACT]. (3) India surcharge is ADDITIVE, not multiplicative: total duty = MFN base + surcharge, so ~32% + ~10% central = ~42% of the ex-factory value ~= $2.52 [ESTIMATE, additive-stack]. (4) Freight + MPF/HMF + broker/bond/drayage under the bulk-IOR model add roughly a few dollars amortised per unit [ESTIMATE]. Landed A2 lands as an [ESTIMATE] band, band-centre illustration ~$11 [DOWNGRADED]. For A1 cotton at a similar ex-factory: MFN is cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% [FACT] (NEVER the discredited ~7%) + ~10% surcharge additive ~= ~26.5%. The ~32% MMF wall erases acrylic's ~$0.5-1 ex-factory lead, so landed A1 (cotton) ~= A2 (acrylic) < A3 — the duty inversion. Crucial confidence note: A1~=A2 is a DIRECTIONAL inversion of a band, robust because it is FACT-anchored on the duty trio, NOT a to-the-cent hard equality, because both ex-factory legs rest on the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate. Cotton is the duty-friendly anchor.

It loses money on the FIRST order (~-$2 to -$47 [ESTIMATE]) because (a) its landed cost is NOT meaningfully below cotton after the ~32% MMF duty, and (b) it carries a FULL CAC against the lowest price ceiling. Precise attribution: the durable driver of the loss is the $55 price ceiling absorbing a full per-order CAC — it is a packaging fact, not a fibre fact; the 32% duty is what removes A2's supposed cost edge but the price-ceiling-vs-full-CAC is what sinks the first order. I do NOT over-correct into 'A2 is structurally dead': A2 is fine and correct as a bundle-filler inside a ~$120-150 AOV 2-unit bundle (which amortises one CAC and one ship), and dead ONLY as a standalone hero. The instruction is: A2 bundle-filler, never standalone lead; lead with A3 / bundles to AOV ~$120-150.

answers.answer: No — a clean CAC test and positive per-order contribution on A3 bundles is necessary but NOT sufficient for a bulk dye-lot PO. Per-order viability does not clear the working-capital trap: cash tied up between paying for dye-lot-MOQ bulk inventory and being paid by customers, stranded for months by ocean lead time + sell-through + returns settlement, overlapping the slow organic-CAC ramp — this is the unmodelled killer and likely TRUE point of death (conflicts_and_dominance 'per-order profitability vs working-capital cash cycle'). Moreover the cash cycle is not even computable yet: G2 (knit+LINK rate) is still [UNKNOWN] and G3 (working-capital funding) is [UNSIZED] — you cannot fund a cycle you cannot size, and it can only be sized after G2 + the dye-MOQ quote. So even with a clean CAC test, committing dye-lot working capital requires the cash gap to be sized and funded first. Per-order profit does NOT equal GO.

answers.answer: Yes, there is a problem, and it changes your duty. Chief weight is by MASS: a garment at 60% acrylic is classified MMF (heading 6110.30.30) at ~32% [FACT], NOT cotton at ~16.5% [FACT] — this is the chief-weight cliff (a 55/45 cotton-acrylic sweater is 'cotton' at ~16.5%, but flip past 50% acrylic and the SAME sweater becomes MMF at ~32%, nearly doubling duty). Labelling it 'cotton' while it is 60% acrylic by mass is a mis-declaration. As Importer of Record, the BRAND owns the duty-misclassification liability [FACT-liability posture] — the supplier's cost-shaving becomes your customs exposure. I will not wave this through. Required control: blend % + tolerance + a fibre-composition check must be written into every PO and confirmed before bulk. Confirm the exact 10-digit HTS line/rate against USITC HTS / CBP / a licensed customs broker; I flag the exposure but give no individualized customs counsel.
answers.grounded_in: capabilities[0]/[5]; glossary 'chief-weight cliff' and 'Importer of Record (IOR)'; escalation_triggers[1] (chief-weight cliff + brand is IOR -> flag); boundaries (never wave through blend-drift/IOR misclassification); competency_questions_covered final item
